placements.title: Nothing ships until its provenance is proven
placements.frame: What must a release show about where it came from before it is allowed to reach staging or production, and what has the organization seen go wrong that makes it insist?
placements.why: The position carries the CTO's rule (a signed release manifest on every Meridian deployment), its scope (staging and production), its owner, and the incident that prompted it. Release provenance is a subject future envelopes will keep feeding, and the leaf rests on the rule and its rationale, not on the incident count. The graph has no existing leaf, so this is a new standalone mint.

mints.name: UnsignedArtifactsPromptedTheSignedManifestGate

mints.why: The CTO says the two unsigned artifacts that reached staging last quarter are 'the whole reason for the gate', which draws the line from incident to decision directly.

mints.why: The gate, its scope across staging and production, and its named owner are one subject that later release-train decisions will keep returning to.
